source_text.body:
Let an agent control a garden using a lakehouse
The author gave an agent a data lakehouse and control of their garden; the post is only a headline, so details are not stated.
·
Nov 8, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
Javier de la Torre put eleven Ecowitt sensors and a Reolink camera on a two-square-metre bed. Both stream into a LakehouseBox catalog of Iceberg tables, set up by prompting an agent. A hosted agent runs at 08:45 each day, checks readings, forecast and photos, and emails a short note. It changes watering through an old Android phone that taps the Rain Bird app.
How it went
About four million readings were collected in seven weeks. The agent adjusts watering and often decides to do nothing. The camera missed caterpillar damage, which close-up phone photos caught. Whether the broccoli improves is still unknown.
Worth knowing
The watering limits (at most 20% change, 1 to 15 minutes) sit only in the agent's prompt. The author wants them enforced in the actuator instead. The camera stored about 3 GB of the 5 GB free plan.
Try it yourself
with
OpenClaw
Copy prompt
I want to automate my garden at [location/type of garden]. Read the sensor or data sources I give you ([e.g. soil moisture sensor, weather API, watering log]), then propose a simple watering and care schedule based on that data. Start by showing me the plan and the data it relies on; do not trigger any device such as a valve or sprinkler until I approve each action.
Original source: https://jatorre.github.io/garden/
